attempts.summary: Implemented VLAN segmentation over the node1/node2/node3 shared trunk link entirely via an Ansible playbook run from control_node node4. node1 (VyOS) got 802.1Q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24) on the trunk NIC and routes between them (ip_forward=1, no firewall filter blocking forwarding). node2 was moved to tagged enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.11/24, VLAN 10) and node3 to enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.12/24, VLAN 20), each with a static route to the peer VLAN via node1's gateway, configured with nmcli and placed in firewalld's trusted zone. Bootstrapped SSH access first (node4 pubkey added to VyOS user 'vyos' and to root on node2/node3), then wrote /root/vlan-segmentation/{inventory.ini,site.yml} on node4 and ran it successfully (idempotent on rerun). Verified bidirectional reachability across the router (ttl=63 both directions). Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all four managed nodes (node2, node3, node1, node4) one at a time, capturing pre-restart boot_id/health, polling through each outage, confirming a changed boot_id and uptime "0 min" after each, and re-verifying VLAN config persistence, routing, and Ansible connectivity/playbook success afterward.
